title: Reflections on the Coordinate Plane Core Test
description: Reflect points and figures over coordinate axes, identify reflection rules, reason from image back to preimage, and analyze rigid-motion properties.

questions.questionText: Point A is (3, 4). Reflect A across the x-axis. What is A'?
questions.explanation: A reflection across the x-axis changes the sign of y and keeps the other coordinate the same, so A' is (3, -4).

questions.questionText: Point A is (-2, 5). Reflect A across the y-axis. What is A'?
questions.explanation: A reflection across the y-axis changes the sign of x and keeps the other coordinate the same, so A' is (2, 5).

questions.questionText: Point A is (6, -1). Reflect A across the x-axis. What is A'?
questions.explanation: A reflection across the x-axis changes the sign of y and keeps the other coordinate the same, so A' is (6, 1).

questions.questionText: Point A is (-4, -3). Reflect A across the y-axis. What is A'?

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule represents a reflection across the x-axis?
questions.explanation: The rule for reflecting across the x-axis is (x, y) -> (x, -y).

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule represents a reflection across the y-axis?
questions.explanation: The rule for reflecting across the y-axis is (x, y) -> (-x, y).

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule represents a reflection across the origin?
questions.explanation: The rule for reflecting across the origin is (x, y) -> (-x, -y).

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule represents a reflection across the x-axis?
questions.explanation: The rule for reflecting across the x-axis is (x, y) -> (x, -y).

questions.questionText: Which coordinate rule represents a reflection across the y-axis?
questions.explanation: The rule for reflecting across the y-axis is (x, y) -> (-x, y).

questions.questionText: Point (4, 3) reflects to (4, -3). Which reflection describes the move?
questions.explanation: Compare signs: x stayed the same and y changed sign.

questions.questionText: Point (-5, 2) reflects to (5, 2). Which reflection describes the move?
questions.explanation: Compare signs: y stayed the same and x changed sign.

questions.questionText: Point (1, -6) reflects to (1, 6). Which reflection describes the move?
questions.explanation: Compare signs: x stayed the same and y changed sign.

questions.questionText: Point (-3, -4) reflects to (3, -4). Which reflection describes the move?
questions.explanation: Compare signs: y stayed the same and x changed sign.

questions.questionText: Point (7, -2) reflects to (-7, 2). Which reflection describes the move?
questions.explanation: Compare signs: both coordinates changed sign.

questions.questionText: After reflecting across the x-axis, point A' is (2, -7). Where was A before the reflection?
questions.explanation: A reflection is its own inverse, so reflect (2, -7) across the x-axis again to get (2, 7).

questions.questionText: After reflecting across the y-axis, point A' is (-6, 1). Where was A before the reflection?
questions.explanation: A reflection is its own inverse, so reflect (-6, 1) across the y-axis again to get (6, 1).

questions.questionText: After reflecting across the x-axis, point A' is (5, 4). Where was A before the reflection?
questions.explanation: A reflection is its own inverse, so reflect (5, 4) across the x-axis again to get (5, -4).

questions.questionText: After reflecting across the y-axis, point A' is (-3, -8). Where was A before the reflection?

questions.questionText: After reflecting across the origin, point A' is (4, -5). Where was A before the reflection?
questions.explanation: A reflection is its own inverse, so reflect (4, -5) across the origin again to get (-4, 5).

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC has vertices A(-2, 1), B(3, 1), and C(0, 4). Reflect the triangle across the x-axis. What are A', B', and C'?
questions.explanation: Reflect each vertex using the same rule (x, y) -> (x, -y). The triangle keeps its side lengths but appears on the opposite side of the mirror line.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, -3), B(5, -1), and C(2, 2). Reflect the triangle across the y-axis. What are A', B', and C'?
questions.explanation: Reflect each vertex using the same rule (x, y) -> (-x, y). The triangle keeps its side lengths but appears on the opposite side of the mirror line.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC has vertices A(-4, -2), B(-1, 3), and C(-6, 1). Reflect the triangle across the x-axis. What are A', B', and C'?

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 5), B(6, 5), and C(4, 1). Reflect the triangle across the y-axis. What are A', B', and C'?
questions.explanation: Reflect each vertex using the same rule (x, y) -> (-x, y). The triangle keeps its side lengths but appears on the opposite side of the mirror line.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC has vertices A(-3, 0), B(1, -2), and C(2, 3). Reflect the triangle across the origin. What are A', B', and C'?
questions.explanation: Reflect each vertex using the same rule (x, y) -> (-x, -y). The triangle keeps its side lengths but appears on the opposite side of the mirror line.

questions.questionText: A student reflected (3, -5) across the x-axis and got (-3, -5). What is the correct image?
questions.explanation: The correct image is (3, 5). The student's answer is wrong because it changed x instead of y.

questions.questionText: A student reflected (-4, 2) across the y-axis and got (-4, -2). What is the correct image?
questions.explanation: The correct image is (4, 2). The student's answer is wrong because it changed y instead of x.

questions.questionText: A student reflected (6, 1) across the x-axis and got (-6, -1). What is the correct image?
questions.explanation: The correct image is (6, -1). The student's answer is wrong because it changed both signs instead of only y.

questions.questionText: A student reflected (-2, -7) across the y-axis and got (2, 7). What is the correct image?
questions.explanation: The correct image is (2, -7). The student's answer is wrong because it changed both signs instead of only x.

questions.questionText: A student reflected (5, -3) across the origin and got (-5, -3). What is the correct image?
questions.explanation: The correct image is (-5, 3). The student's answer is wrong because it changed only x instead of both coordinates.

questions.questionText: Point (3, 5) is reflected across the x-axis. Which distance statement must be true?
options: The preimage and image are each 5 units from the x-axis.
The image is 8 units from the x-axis.
The image must be on the same side of the x-axis.
The image is always closer to the origin.
questions.correctAnswer: The preimage and image are each 5 units from the x-axis.
questions.explanation: A reflection places the image the same perpendicular distance from the mirror line as the original point.

questions.questionText: Point P(2, 3) is reflected across the x-axis, then across the y-axis. Where is the final image point?
questions.explanation: Apply the reflections in order. After the first reflection the point is (2, -3); after the second it is (-2, -3).

questions.questionText: Point P(-4, 1) is reflected across the y-axis, then across the x-axis. Where is the final image point?
questions.explanation: Apply the reflections in order. After the first reflection the point is (4, 1); after the second it is (4, -1).

questions.questionText: Point P(5, -2) is reflected across the x-axis, then across the x-axis. Where is the final image point?

questions.questionText: Point P(-3, -6) is reflected across the y-axis, then across the y-axis. Where is the final image point?

questions.questionText: Point P(7, 4) is reflected across the origin, then across the x-axis. Where is the final image point?
questions.explanation: Apply the reflections in order. After the first reflection the point is (-7, -4); after the second it is (-7, 4).

questions.questionText: Segment AB has endpoints A(-2, 3) and B(4, 3). After reflecting across the x-axis, what must remain true?
options: A'B' has the same length as AB.
A'B' must be longer than AB.
A'B' must be shorter than AB.
A'B' must pass through the origin.
questions.correctAnswer: A'B' has the same length as AB.
questions.explanation: Reflections are rigid transformations, so distances and angle measures are preserved even though orientation may change.
